title: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF
claim: Prior methods regularize toward a fixed reference and a local trust region separately, blocking high-reward regions; unifying both expands reachable space and improves the trade-off.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; two geometric diagrams then a Pareto plot
description: Three panels. Panels (a) and (b) are parallel geometric sketches. Each has a blue 'Reward Hacking' band at the top with a star marking the optimal policy, a large dome showing the KL penalty region around the reference policy π0 at the bottom, and a smaller circle showing the clipping region around the current policy πt. A curved blue arrow runs from π0 up to πt. In (a), the dome is gray and the circle only partly overlaps it, so the high-reward star π* stays outside the reachable area. In (b), the region is peach and the circle merges with the dome. A red 'Search Expansion' label points to the new reachable area that now contains the star. Panel (c) is a scatter plot with fitted curves of reward against KL divergence to π0. It compares PPO in blue with Dual-PPO in pink and Dual-PPO-Clip in green. The two dual variants sit above PPO. The eye goes first to the contrasting gray and peach diagrams.
caption: Dual-KL regularization enables exploration beyond reference policy support. (a) PPO-based RLHF uses policy ratio clipping relative to πt for stable optimization and KL divergence penalty relative to π0 for reference regularization. High-reward regions remain unexplored when they lack sufficient support under the reference policy. (b) Our approach unifies stable optimization and reference regularization, enabling flexible trade-offs between the two mechanisms. This allows the policy to expand into high-reward regions previously inaccessible due to limited reference support, achieving better alignment when substantial behavioral changes are required. (c) Empirical validation on Anthropic-Helpfulness dataset: incorporating dual-KL penalties in advantage estimation improves the reward-KL Pareto frontier over standard PPO for both Dual-PPO variants.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has advanced alignment capabilities significantly but remains hindered by two core challenges: \textbf{reward hacking} and \textbf{stable optimization}. Current solutions independently address these issues through separate regularization strategies, specifically a KL-divergence penalty against a supervised fine-tuned model ($Ï_0$) to mitigate reward hacking, and policy ratio clipping towards the current policy ($Ï_t$) to promote stable alignment. However, the implicit trade-off arising from simultaneously regularizing towards both $Ï_0$ and $Ï_t$ remains under-explored. In this paper, we introduce a unified regularization approach that explicitly balances the objectives of preventing reward hacking and maintaining stable policy updates. Our simple yet principled alignment objective yields a weighted supervised fine-tuning loss with a superior trade-off, which demonstrably improves both alignment results and implementation complexity. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks validate that our method consistently outperforms RLHF and online preference learning methods, achieving enhanced alignment performance and stability.
